summary: 67-year-old man whose known right inguinal hernia became irreducible 5 hours ago; mildly tender, no skin change, no obstruction, normal vitals, lactate 1.3. WSES: no signs of strangulation, so gentle reduction may be tried, then repair; mesh in a clean field.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Groin lump that will not go back
inputs.hpi: Known right groin hernia for 2 years, always reducible. Five hours ago it came out while lifting and will not go back. Aching 4/10, not getting worse. Passing flatus, bowels opened this morning. No vomiting. No fever.

exam.abdomen: Abdomen soft, not distended, non-tender, normal bowel sounds. Right inguinoscrotal hernia, irreducible, mildly tender, no overlying erythema or warmth, no peritonism.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Incarcerated right inguinal hernia without strangulation
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Irreducible inguinal hernia (right), incarcerated for 5 h. No clinical or biochemical signs of strangulation (lactate 1.3, WCC 9.1, no skin change, no obstruction). Gentle reduction under analgesia, then repair.

emergencyLevel.note: An irreducible hernia needs same-day surgical assessment: strangulation cannot be excluded without it.

mustInclude.note: WSES 2017: lactate (with CPK, D-dimer) helps predict strangulation.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: The inguinal_hernia protocol lists FBC, U&E only; no lactate/CPK (WSES strangulation markers) anywhere in the web outputs.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add lactate (± CPK, D-dimer) and CT when strangulation is uncertain to the hernia protocols for irreducible hernias.

mustInclude.note: Either gentle reduction followed by early repair, or emergency repair.
WSES 2017: synthetic mesh repair is recommended in a clean surgical field (no bowel resection).

mustExclude.note: Watchful waiting applies to reducible minimally symptomatic hernias only.

dxVariant.note: The documented plan must be the incarcerated-hernia plan (reduction attempt, then early repair), not the elective plan.
dxVariant.proposedFix: Match detectKeywords on word boundaries, check the most severe variant first (strangulated → incarcerated → reducible), and add negative look-behind for 'ir'/'non-' ("irreducible" contains "reducible"); "bethesda vi" contains "bethesda v".

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias (2017 update)
guideline.section: Diagnosis of strangulation (clinical signs, lactate, CPK, D-dimer, CT); timing of surgery; manual reduction only without strangulation; mesh in clean (CDC I) and clean-contaminated fields
guideline.citation: Birindelli A, Sartelli M, Di Saverio S, et al. 2017 update of the WSES guidelines for emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias. World J Emerg Surg. 2017;12:37.

guideline.name: HerniaSurge — International guidelines for groin hernia management
guideline.section: Diagnosis (clinical examination, ultrasound for uncertain swellings); watchful waiting in minimally symptomatic men; mesh repair (Lichtenstein, TEP/TAPP); groin hernia in women; femoral hernia; emergency repair
guideline.citation: HerniaSurge Group. International guidelines for groin hernia management. Hernia. 2018;22:1–165.

rationale: Base emergency hernia case. The assessment is phrased the way surgeons write it ("Irreducible inguinal hernia (right)"), which also tests keyword-based variant detection. Negatives in the HPI ("No vomiting. No fever.") exercise negation handling.
